source: Invest Like the Best — Why the markets are pricing AI wrong: July 2026 AI/semis selloff, private inference cloud, old-GPU repricing, ~$700B Blackwell/Rubin credit gap
summary: Contracted GPU compute is trading at a massive discount to spot market; as contracts roll off and reprice higher, hyperscaler operating cash flows will accelerate sharply
summary_extended: Baker argues that GPU compute contracts signed in 2024-2025 are now massively underpriced relative to current spot market rates, creating a significant earnings acceleration catalyst as those contracts roll off and reprice higher. The evidence is concrete: a startup Baker spoke to that day was paying ~$2/GPU-hour on a Blackwell cluster and expected to pay just under $4 for the same cluster 7 months later (a ~50-60% increase), while one inference cloud publicly stated it expects to pay 100% more when its Blackwell contract expires. Baker's thesis is that the entire contracted installed base of GPU compute — primarily owned and operated by hyperscalers — is currently under-earning relative to spot, and as multi-year contracts roll off, hyperscaler operating cash flows will accelerate materially. The investment implication is to be long the major hyperscalers (Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, and Google) who own and lease out large GPU fleets, as their compute revenue and margins will reprice sharply upward over the medium term. This is a contrarian view because the market in mid-2026 was pricing AI infrastructure as a cost burden rather than a repricing revenue opportunity.
detail: In 2024-2025, everyone assumed GPU prices would decline slowly or precipitously. Instead, old GPU prices are going vertical in 2026. A startup Baker spoke to that day was paying ~$2/GPU-hour on a Blackwell cluster and expected to pay just under $4 for the same cluster 7 months later — a 50-60% increase. One inference cloud publicly stated they expect to pay 100% more when their Blackwell contract expires. This means the entire contracted installed base of compute is under-earning relative to spot, and as contracts roll off, hyperscaler operating cash flows will accelerate materially.
confidence_evidence: Baker provides specific anecdotal data points (startup paying $2 going to $4, inference cloud expecting 100% increase), frames this as the central bull case, and quantifies the impact on operating cash flows
